label: Functional Analysis
notes: Open the chapter. Functional analysis studies infinite-dimensional spaces of functions and the linear operators acting on them. The deck follows PDF pages 51 through 54 and introduces Hilbert spaces, bounded linear operators, adjoints, and the spectral viewpoint that the next chapter develops in full.

label: Hilbert Spaces of Functions
notes: Recall that a Hilbert space is a complete inner-product space and emphasize the function-space examples: square-integrable functions form an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. Orthonormal bases let any function be expanded as a series of coefficients, the analytic basis for Fourier and spectral methods.

label: Linear Operators
notes: Introduce bounded linear operators between Hilbert spaces and the operator norm. Boundedness is equivalent to continuity. Neural network layers, convolutions, and integral transforms are operators, so understanding their norms governs stability and the conditioning of learning.

label: Adjoints and Self-Adjointness
notes: Define the adjoint operator via the inner product and the special class of self-adjoint operators. Self-adjoint operators have real spectra and orthogonal eigenfunctions, the property that makes the Laplacian and graph operators diagonalizable and underlies spectral convolution.

label: Toward Spectral Theory
notes: Preview spectral theory. For compact self-adjoint operators the spectral theorem provides a complete orthonormal set of eigenfunctions with real eigenvalues. This decomposition turns differential and graph operators into simple multiplication in the eigenbasis, the foundation of spectral networks.

label: Recap
notes: Close the chapter. Hilbert function spaces host infinite-dimensional analysis, bounded operators are the continuous linear maps, adjoints and self-adjointness give real spectra, and the spectral theorem prepares the diagonalization developed in Chapter 06 spectral theory.
